name: Mythology trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about myths and legends from cultures around the world. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Who is the king of the gods in Greek mythology?
items.explain: Zeus was the king of the twelve Olympian gods and the supreme god in Greek religion.

source.title: The 12 Olympian Gods - World History Encyclopedia

items.question: On which mountain were the twelve Olympian gods said to live?
items.explain: The Olympians were the twelve principal Greek gods, and they were thought to live on Mount Olympus.

items.question: In Greek myth, which part of Achilles' body was his one vulnerable spot?
items.explain: Achilles' mother dipped him in the River Styx but held him by the heel, so the heel was the only part left vulnerable. He died from an arrow wound there.

items.question: Which Greek hero beheaded the Gorgon Medusa?
items.explain: Perseus killed Medusa, the only mortal Gorgon, by cutting off her head.

items.question: In Greek myth, a glance from Medusa turned onlookers into what?
items.explain: Medusa was a Gorgon whose gaze turned anyone who looked at her to stone.

items.question: Which Greek hero killed the Minotaur in the Labyrinth with Ariadne's help?
items.explain: Theseus volunteered as one of the sacrificial victims in order to kill the Minotaur. Ariadne helped him escape the Labyrinth.

items.question: Which Greek hero is credited with devising the Trojan Horse trick?
items.explain: The Trojan Horse was a ruse devised by the Greek hero Odysseus to get inside Troy and finally conquer it.

source.title: Fall of Troy Marks End of Trojan War

items.question: Which epic poem by Homer centres on Achilles' quarrel with Agamemnon during the Trojan War?
items.explain: Homer's Iliad centres on Achilles' quarrel with Agamemnon late in the war and ends with the death of the Trojan hero Hector.

items.question: Which Trojan prince's abduction of Helen is said to have started the Trojan War?
items.explain: In the myth, Paris, the Trojan prince, carried off Helen, and this started the war. He later killed Achilles with an arrow.

source.title: The myth of the Trojan War

items.question: How many labours did King Eurystheus set Hercules in the traditional cycle?
items.explain: The Labours of Hercules were later arranged in a standard cycle of twelve tasks assigned by King Eurystheus.

items.question: Hercules wore the skin of which beast after slaying it as the first of his labours?
items.explain: The first labour was the slaying of the Nemean lion, and Hercules wore its skin afterwards.

items.question: Which Titan stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans?
items.explain: In Hesiod's account Prometheus stole fire from heaven. Zeus took revenge by sending Pandora to Prometheus' brother Epimetheus.

items.question: In the original Greek story, what was Pandora's famous "box"?
items.explain: The Greek word was pithos, meaning a large jar. It was later rendered as "box" in a Latin retelling.

items.question: In the Greek myth, why did Icarus fall into the sea?
answers: He grew tired and let go
The sun melted the wax on his wings
items.correct: The sun melted the wax on his wings
items.explain: Icarus got carried away and flew too close to the sun. The heat melted the wax holding his wings together.

source.title: 12 of the Best Stories from Greek Myth

items.question: King Midas was famed for turning everything he touched into what?
items.explain: The myth of King Midas and the golden touch tells of a king who turned everything he touched into gold.

source.title: 12 of the Best Stories from Greek Myth

items.question: Which Roman god corresponds to the Greek king of the gods, Zeus?
items.explain: The Roman equivalent of Zeus is Jupiter, who, like Zeus, ruled all the Roman gods.

source.title: Greek and Roman Mythology - Mythology - LibGuides at Touro University-NY

items.question: Which Roman goddess corresponds to the Greek goddess Aphrodite?
items.explain: Venus is the Roman goddess of love and beauty, the counterpart of the Greek Aphrodite.

source.title: List of Roman Gods and their Greek Equivalents - World History Edu

items.question: Which Roman god was the god of war?
items.explain: Mars is the Roman god of war, the counterpart of the Greek Ares.

source.title: Myths and Astronomy - World Mythology - LibGuides at St. Louis County Library

items.question: Which Greek god, the counterpart of Rome's Mercury, was messenger of the gods and wore winged sandals?
items.explain: Mercury is the Roman messenger god with winged sandals, and his Greek name is Hermes.

source.title: Myths and Astronomy - World Mythology - LibGuides at St. Louis County Library

items.question: Venus was the mother of which Roman god of love?
items.explain: Venus is described as the mother of Cupid, the Roman god of love.

source.title: Myths and Astronomy - World Mythology - LibGuides at St. Louis County Library

items.question: Which Greek god ruled the underworld, known to the Romans as Pluto?
items.explain: Hades was the Greek god of the underworld, and his Roman counterpart was Pluto.

source.title: List of Roman Gods and their Greek Equivalents - World History Edu

items.question: According to Hesiod, from which part of Zeus did Athena emerge?
items.explain: In Hesiod's account, Athena came out of the head of Zeus himself.

items.question: Which Olympian is the Greek god of wine and merriment?
items.explain: Dionysus was the Greek god of wine and merriment, and he is often counted among the twelve Olympians.

source.title: The 12 Olympian Gods - World History Encyclopedia

items.question: Which Greek god ruled the sea and was also linked to earthquakes and horses?
items.explain: Poseidon was the Greek god of the sea, earthquakes and horses. His Roman counterpart is Neptune.

items.question: Which day of the week is named after the Norse god Thor?
items.explain: Thursday comes from "Thor's day". Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday are named after Tyr, Odin and Frigg.

items.question: Which Norse god of thunder wields the hammer Mjölnir?
items.explain: Thor was the thunder god, and his hammer Mjölnir protected both gods and humans.

items.question: Who is the king of the Æsir, the main group of Norse gods?
items.explain: Odin was the king of the Æsir. The Norse believed he decided the fate of every battle.

source.title: 12 most important Norse gods and goddesses in Viking mythology

items.question: Which Norse god is famous as a cunning, shape-shifting trickster?
items.explain: In Norse mythology Loki is a cunning trickster who can change his shape and sex.

items.question: In Norse tradition, which place was Odin believed to live in?
items.explain: Odin was traditionally believed to live in Valhalla, the great hall in Asgard.

items.question: What name do Norse myths give to the eventual end of the world?
items.explain: Norse myths tell of the creation of the world and of its eventual end, which is called Ragnarök.

items.question: Which jackal-headed Egyptian god was associated with mummification?
items.explain: Anubis was the jackal-headed Egyptian god of mummification.

items.question: Which Egyptian god was the sun god and a creator deity?
items.explain: Ra was the creator deity of the Egyptians, god of the sun and keeper of cosmic order.

items.question: In the Egyptian myth, which god kills his brother Osiris?
items.explain: Osiris was killed by his brother Set. His wife Isis then restored him with help from Anubis and Thoth.

source.title: The Egyptian Mythology Story of Osiris

items.question: In the Osiris myth, which goddess restores her husband's body so that he can father Horus?
items.explain: Isis restores the body of her husband Osiris, which allows him to father their son Horus after his death.

items.question: Which Egyptian god became the ruler of the underworld and the afterlife?
items.explain: In the creation myths Osiris became the ruler of the underworld, taking over the role Anubis once held.

items.question: In the Hindu trimurti, which god is the destroyer and transformer?
items.explain: The trimurti is the triad of Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

items.question: Which Hindu deity is readily identified by his elephant head?
items.explain: Ganesha is one of the best-known and most worshipped Hindu deities, and he is readily identified by his elephant head.

items.question: Which member of the Hindu trimurti descends to earth as avatars to restore cosmic order?
items.explain: Vishnu is said to descend in the form of an avatar to restore cosmic order. The Dashavatara are his ten primary avatars.

items.question: What is the name of King Arthur's legendary sword?
items.explain: Geoffrey of Monmouth described Arthur's magic sword, called Caliburn and later Excalibur.

source.title: Was King Arthur a Real Person?

items.question: Which wizard famously tutored and advised the young King Arthur?
items.explain: In the legend Arthur was trained by Merlin the Magician, who also helped him become king.

source.title: Was King Arthur a Real Person?

items.question: What name is given to King Arthur's legendary fortress and court?
items.explain: In the legend Arthur acquired a fortress called Camelot, along with his friend Lancelot.

source.title: Welsh places connected to the King Arthur legend

items.question: Who is King Arthur's queen in the legends?
items.explain: Queen Guinevere is Arthur's wife in the legend. His half-sister Morgan le Fay is a separate character.

source.title: Was King Arthur a Real Person?

items.question: To which magical island was the mortally wounded King Arthur said to be taken to heal?
items.explain: Avalon is the magical island where Arthur's sword was said to be forged. After Mordred wounded him, Arthur was taken there to heal.

source.title: Welsh places connected to the King Arthur legend

items.question: In Irish folklore, whose wailing is said to foretell a coming death?
items.explain: The banshee is a female spirit whose wailing is said to foretell a coming death.

items.question: Which child-sized Irish fairy is said to hoard pots of gold?
items.explain: The leprechaun is a mischievous, child-sized fairy in Irish folklore with a habit of hoarding pots of gold.

items.question: Which part-divine king of Uruk searches for immortality in an ancient Mesopotamian epic?
items.explain: The Epic of Gilgamesh follows the king of Uruk, who is part god and part human, in his search for immortality.

items.question: Which goddess is the sun deity of Japanese Shinto mythology and the ancestor of the imperial family?
items.explain: Amaterasu is the primary kami of Shinto, representing the sun, and the mythological ancestor of the Japanese imperial family.

items.question: In Japanese myth, which divine pair stirred the sea with a jeweled spear to create the first land?
items.explain: Izanagi and Izanami stood on the floating bridge of heaven and stirred the ocean with a jeweled spear. This created the first landmass.

items.question: By what name is the Aztec god Quetzalcoatl commonly known?
items.explain: Quetzalcoatl's name means "quetzal-bird snake", which is why he is called the Feathered Serpent. The Maya knew the same deity as Kukulcan.

source.title: Of Serpents and Deities: The Many Meanings of Snakes in Mesoamerica

items.question: Which stone-born Chinese mythological character, known as the Monkey King, stars in Journey to the West?
items.explain: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, first appeared in the 16th-century novel Journey to the West. He is born from a stone that produces a magical egg.
